::: {.lead-intro}
Not every map has to answer a question. These are the ones I make because I like how they look, mostly on weekends, often after a week of checking numbers. I'll be adding more over time.
:::

## 💘 For Valentine's

A made-up map of how to get to someone's heart: leave the Sea of Overthinking, take the long way round through the little things, and say sorry at the bridge. ## In colour

### Watercolour cities (2026)

In 2022 I made a land cover map of Gorton and Abbey Hey in Manchester, styled with John Nelson's watercolour approach in ArcGIS Pro. Years later I recreated the look outside Pro, in Python, starting with Elbasan, Albania, where I'm from, and then Athens. Both use the Copernicus Urban Atlas 2021, reclassified into the same blue, green and grey legend I used in the IGNITION project.

::: {layout-ncol=2}
![**Elbasan.** The old town around the castle, Parku Rinia by the stadium, the hill of Krasta and the Shkumbin river with its gravel banks, inside an irregular circle around the city. Data: Copernicus Urban Atlas 2021 (EEA / Copernicus Land Monitoring Service).](img/elbasan.jpg){group="colour" fig-alt="Watercolour land cover map of Elbasan, Albania"}

![**Athens and Piraeus.** The same style across the Athens basin down to the sea at Piraeus. Data: Copernicus Urban Atlas 2021 (EEA / Copernicus Land Monitoring Service).](img/athens-piraeus.jpg){group="colour" fig-alt="Watercolour land cover map of Athens and Piraeus"}
:::

Urban Atlas maps land *use*, not land cover, so there are judgement calls: Krasta, a wooded hill, has the same code as a small town park.

### Old-style Peloponnese (2026)

A few years ago I made an old-style map of the Peloponnese in ArcGIS Pro. I made it again without Pro, building the relief from my own 25 m contours and adding the sea and coastline from EMODnet Bathymetry, on a parchment-style background with old-style lettering.

![**Peloponnese.** Relief from 25 m contours. Sea and coastline: EMODnet Bathymetry.](img/peloponnese-vintage.jpg){group="colour" fig-alt="Old-style map of the Peloponnese on parchment, with shaded mountains, pale blue sea and serif lettering for the towns, gulfs and summits"}

<p class="links">Prints are available to buy: see the <a href="../about.qmd">About</a> page to get in touch.</p>

### The Netherlands, land of windmills (2026)

The same old-style look as the Peloponnese, but in happier colours. Every one of the 1,231 traditional windmills mapped in OpenStreetMap has its own little windmill on the map. The mint and turquoise land is below sea level: a lot of it was drained by windmills in the first place.

![**The Netherlands, land of windmills.** Heights: EMODnet DTM. Windmills: © OpenStreetMap contributors.](img/netherlands-windmills.jpg){group="colour" fig-alt="Old-style map of the Netherlands in bright colours, with mint-green land below sea level, sky-blue sea and over a thousand small red windmills, with Kinderdijk, Zaanse Schans and Schiedam picked out"}

<p class="links">Prints are available to buy: see the <a href="../about.qmd">About</a> page to get in touch.</p>
